research_question: When the frozen 48-token W path differs from WF, did the constructive completion planner reject a token even though the remainder of the already observed W path is itself a deterministic-verifier-accepted certificate inside the remaining native-token budget?
registration_boundary: The complete test128 generation, scores, gate, and the identities of the two changed rows were known before this diagnostic was registered. The audit therefore replays all 128 W rows and is descriptive failure analysis, not confirmatory evidence for a repaired method.

audit.replay: Replay the exact W native-token path through the frozen WF admission rule. At every rejected token, independently replay the observed residual W suffix from its successor state through the deterministic verifier and require accepting EOS within the remaining budget before calling the event a constructive-planner false negative.

claim_boundary: This post-hoc audit may establish that the frozen constructive proposer missed certificates which the unchanged deterministic verifier accepts. It cannot establish the effect, quality, or population behavior of any later repair; that requires a newly registered held-out generation protocol.
